newsitem.title: EGYPT: Turkish goods ship catches fire in Red Sea.
newsitem.headline: Turkish goods ship catches fire in Red Sea.

text.p: Firefighters fought for 12 hours to put out a fire on a Turkish ship carrying steel near Egypt's Red Sea coast, port sources said on Tuesday.

The Red Sea Port Authority sources said the incident took place on Monday about 163 km (100 miles) south of the Gulf of Suez. The ship, called Tahir Kiran, was on its way from Istanbul to the Saudi port of Jeddah with 25,957 tonnes of steel aboard.
Eight of the ship's 26 crew members were taken to hospital for treatment of suffocation, the sources said.
Oil company tugs with firefighters on board rushed to the ship's aid after it contacted the Red Sea Port Authority requesting help, they added.
They said they had notified the ship's owner Kiran Shipping Company Group in Istanbul but said it was too early to estimate the amount of damage caused by the fire.
Tugs would later on Tuesday begin pulling the ship back closer to the Gulf of Suez where it can be fixed, the sources said.
